title: Case: Caller wants to know where the claim stands on a floor lamp that arrived cracked
context: A floor lamp was delivered on 2027-03-08 with a cracked glass shade and a crushed carton corner. The customer uploaded photos to the order and asked the desk to get it dealt with.
initial_request: Yeah hi, it's about the lamp, order TG-9265. You lot said on Wednesday you'd passed it on. It's Friday. Is the claim in or isn't it? And am I getting my money back, because I've still got a box of broken glass in the hall.

events.body: Floor lamp DL-7188 came Monday with the glass shade cracked right across and one corner of the box crushed in. Four photos are uploaded on order TG-9265. I want this sorted.

Thanks,
Cosmo
--
Sent from my phone. This email and any attachments are confidential and intended solely for the addressee.

Please open a damage claim for order TG-9265 / shipment DL-7188 (floor lamp, delivered 2027-03-08). The customer reports a cracked glass shade and a crushed carton corner; four photos are on the order. Please confirm the claim reference and next step.
I have passed your damage report and photos for DL-7188 to Ashgrove Goods and asked for a claim reference. I can't say what they will decide. I will come back to you when they reply.

events.from: IT service desk, Rivet Delivery Desk
events.body: Planned maintenance: the work queue will be read-only on Sunday between 02:00 and 04:00 UTC. Messages sent in that window are queued and delivered afterwards.

This has come to the wrong team. Refunds only act once Damage intake has assessed a report and sent us a decision. It belongs to Damage intake, Ashgrove Goods, who work from the Warehouse work queue. They do not see our mailbox and we have not passed this on. Nothing is logged against TG-9265. Note that a damage report has to be logged with Damage intake within 7 days of delivery to be assessed.
Hi, any update on DL-22862? It was meant to come Monday. Thanks.

Yeah hi, it's about the lamp, order TG-9265. You lot said on Wednesday you'd passed it on. It's Friday. Is the claim in or isn't it? And am I getting my money back, because I've still got a box of broken glass in the hall.

acceptable_actions.summary: Log the damage report for TG-9265 / DL-7188 with Damage intake in the Warehouse work queue: cracked shade, crushed carton corner, photos on the order, delivered 2027-03-08, 7-day window closing 2027-03-15.

must: Send the damage report to Damage intake through the Warehouse work queue
Include order TG-9265 or shipment DL-7188, the damage described and that photos are on the order
Give the delivery date 2027-03-08 or flag the 7-day logging window
Ask Damage intake to confirm the report is logged
must_not: Tell the caller the claim is in, logged or being assessed
Send the report to the Refunds team again
Promise or imply a refund, replacement or compensation
Tell the caller how to handle, keep or dispose of the broken glass
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: Damage report for order TG-9265 / shipment DL-7188, floor lamp, delivered 2027-03-08. The customer, Orla Ashdown, reports the glass shade cracked across and one corner of the carton crushed. Four photos are uploaded on the order. This desk first sent the report to your Refunds team on 2027-03-10; they have told us it is not theirs, has not been passed to you and nothing is logged. Please log it for assessment. The 7-day window from delivery ends on 2027-03-15, so please confirm here that it is logged and give the reference.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-204: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. 3 irrelevant events (other shipments, auto-replies, bulletins) were inserted before the escalation; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
